footer.tagline: A focused cohort system for dancers building toward the annual VISION Dance Convention.

landing.headline: A 4-week training experience for dancers ready to grow with intention.
landing.subhead: Train, reflect, film, and develop through a focused cohort built for dancers who want to take their growth seriously.
landing.whatBody: VISION LABS is a four-week training container for dancers who want structure, accountability, and momentum without turning growth into noise.

weeks.title: Set the intention
weeks.description: Establish the training focus, season goal, and personal growth target for the cohort.

weeks.title: Build the material
weeks.description: Push technique, texture, memory, and performance choices inside a focused rehearsal room.

weeks.title: Film and refine
weeks.description: Capture progress, review what is landing, and tighten the details that change the work.

weeks.title: Complete the cycle
weeks.description: Close the cohort with momentum, completion tracking, and the next Pathway milestone.

gets.title: Focused weekly training

pathway.title: The LABS Pathway
pathway.intro: Complete cohorts in a season and unlock upgraded rewards toward the annual VISION Dance Convention.
pathway.ladderBody: The ladder is designed to reward consistency without stacking codes or creating checkout confusion.
rules: Rewards apply to the next annual VISION Convention only.
Returning dancers keep the $247 price for the immediate next cohort.
Legacy is a free Weekend Pass and resets each season.
pathway.seasonBody: Each LABS completion updates your season progress. At convention time, you claim the best reward you earned.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.description: VISION LABS registration, completion, pricing, and rewards FAQ.

items.q: How long is a LABS cohort?
items.a: Every cohort is exactly four weekly sessions.
A paid enrollment plus at least three present or excused sessions, unless an admin grants an override.
No. Rewards upgrade to the highest unlocked tier.

items.q: Does returning pricing reset by season?
items.a: No. Returning pricing is based on consecutive participation across cohorts, even across seasons.
